rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before data; real-skeleton synthetic (five worlds, 10 windows, 2 channels; Amendment 1); 2 natives (whole #38 and #51 main, with 38a and boundary ranks) and 8 replication units; robustness (weekday-stratified splits, first-day drop) and labelled post hoc checks (J-only, h-only, pre-join); 80 estimates rows; confirm.py frozen (SHA-256) and dry-run, not run. Missing: time-varying fits, drivers of the drift, holdout.
rationale.faithfulness: Scored on the claim that stands (periods drift): the HH's own stationarity prediction for #38 failed (the kill), but the drift claim rests on permutation-calibrated tests with synthetic size <= 0.12 and power 1.00 at the drift that matters, robust to weekday strata and the kickoff day, and replicates in 4/8 long units (the rest underpowered). EP drift is unidentifiable. Scorecard A1 B1 C2 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A design rule for anyone fitting swarm models: fit in about one-week windows and report long periods as trajectories; it changes how this project's own phase diagram should be read. A diagnostic, not a lever.

one_line: A goal period is not a stationary NESS: kinetic Ising parameters of activity and talk drift beyond day-split placebo noise inside #38 (R 1.95-2.18, Holm <= 0.008) and #51 (R 2.14-2.17), gradually rather than at step changes, while an 8-day unit shows no drift.

models.note: stationary kinetic Ising within a period rejected in #38 and #51 (drift ratio about 2); holds in the 8-day unit 38a

v2.claim: Goal periods longer than about a week are not stationary: #38 drifts in both activity and talk couplings (half-vs-half ratio 1.95 / 2.18, trend 2.22 / 2.60, Holm ≤ 0.008), gradually rather than at a step; the #51 main body drifts too (2.17 / 2.14), while an 8-day unit (38a) is stationary (power 0.85)

ladder.factor: synthetic size and power on the real skeleton
robust to weekday stratification and dropping the kickoff day

v2.decision: refit models in windows of about a week; a whole long period is not one steady state
